children: New Delhi, Oct. 25 -- Reliance Jio Platforms and Paras Healthcare IPOs witnessed contrasting levels of investor demand, with the former attracting bids worth several lakh crore rupees and the latter closing its subscription with a more modest response. While Jio Platforms' IPO was subscribed 22.19 times, driven by strong institutional participation, Paras Healthcare's public issue was subscribed 2.23 times on the final day of bidding.

The grey market premium (GMP) also points to a sharp difference in listing expectations. Jio Platforms' IPO GMP stood at Rs.250, implying a potential listing gain of around 22.34% over the upper end of its price band, while Paras Healthcare's GMP was Rs.12, indicating a potential gain of 1.73%. Grey market premiums are unofficial indicators and do not guarantee listing performance.
The public issues opened on 21 October and conclude on 23 October, with allotment scheduled for tomorrow (26 October).
Here's a closer look at the subscription figures, investor categories and latest GMP trends for both IPOs.

Reliance Industries-backed Jio Platforms' IPO closed with bids for 22.19 times the shares on offer, as total demand across the public issue and anchor investor placement crossed Rs.7.4 lakh crore. The offering also received nearly 1.39 crore applications, marking an unprecedented response to the digital services company.

By 7 PM on Friday, investors had bid for 438.3 crore shares against 19.75 crore shares on offer, according to exchange data. Bids for the public issue alone exceeded Rs.4.9 lakh crore, excluding the anchor book, while retail demand crossed Rs.25,867 crore.

Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) led the subscription, bidding for 345.8 crore shares against 4.9 crore shares reserved for them. The category was subscribed 70.55 times. Within the QIB segment, domestic financial institutions, including banks, financial institutions and insurers, bid for 152.5 crore shares, while foreign institutional investors bid for 123.9 crore shares. Mutual funds bid for 35.7 crore shares.

The non-institutional investor (NII) category was subscribed 14 times, while retail individual investors subscribed 2.72 times their reserved portion. The shareholder reservation category was subscribed 7.60 times and the employee portion 2.93 times.
The combined demand figure represents the value of shares investors sought across the public issue and anchor placement, not the amount Jio Platforms will raise.

Jio Platforms IPO is a completely new issue of 27 crore shares. At the upper end of the price band it will raise approximately Rs.30,213 crore and command a valuation of around $108 billion. Neither the parent company (Reliance Industries) nor any of its existing shareholders are participating in the offering.

Jio Platforms' IPO GMP stood at Rs.250. Based on the upper end of the reported price band, the estimated listing price was Rs.1,369 per share, implying a potential premium of 22.34% over the IPO price of Rs.1,119.

Over the past 22 sessions, the GMP ranged between Rs.148 and Rs.273, with the latest premium indicating strong grey market listing expectations. However, GMP is an unofficial market indicator and can change before listing.

Paras Healthcare's IPO, which operates hospitals under the Paras Health brand, closed with an overall subscription of 2.23 times on Friday. Investors bid for 2,69,43,714 shares against 1,20,83,331 shares on offer, according to NSE data.

Unlike Jio Platforms, institutional demand was more moderate. The QIB category was subscribed 3.09 times, while retail investors subscribed 2 times their reserved portion. The NII category received bids for 66% of the shares on offer, leaving it undersubscribed.
Paras Healthcare raised Rs.652.5 crore from anchor investors on Monday. Participants in the anchor book included Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, BlackRock and Eastspring Investments.
Paras Healthcare IPO has a fresh issue of equity shares of Rs.500 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of shares of Rs.950 crore by promoter Dharminder Kumar Nagar and investor Commelina Ltd.
It's brought the issue size down from the original Rs.1,800 crore.

Paras Healthcare's IPO GMP stood at Rs.12. Based on the upper end of its price band, the estimated listing price was Rs.705 per share, suggesting a potential gain of 1.73% over the IPO price of Rs.693.

Over the past 12 sessions, the GMP fluctuated between Rs.11 and Rs.96. The latest premium indicates more modest listing expectations than those for Jio Platforms, although actual listing performance may differ from grey market indications.
